function.description: This function is used to create a recommendation model using a given user data and an algorithm type Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_data.description: A data frame of user ratings. Rows represent users, columns represent items, and entries represent user ratings for items

algorithm.description: The algorithm to be used for creating the recommendation model. Collaborative filtering, content-based filtering and hybrid filtering.

matrix_factorization.description: Optional parameter to indicate whether matrix factorization should be used. Default is False.

message.content: Building a front‑end for an e‑commerce site is a multi‑step process that blends design, architecture, and technology choices. Below is a practical roadmap you can follow—feel free to skip or reorder sections based on your team’s expertise and project scope. --- ## 1️⃣ Define Your Requirements & Goals | What | Why | |------|-----| | **Target audience** (mobile vs desktop, regions, devices) | Determines responsive strategy and performance targets | | **Core features** (product catalog, search, filters, cart, checkout, reviews, wishlists, personalization) | Drives component design and API contracts | | **Performance goals** (first paint < 2 s, interactive < 5 s) | Sets optimization priorities | | **Accessibility** (WCAG 2.1 AA) | Ensures inclusivity and legal compliance | | **SEO** (server‑side rendering, structured data) | Improves organic traffic | | **Analytics & tracking** (Google Analytics, heatmaps, conversion funnels) | Enables data‑driven decisions | > **Tip:** Create a “feature backlog” and prioritize with MoSCoW (Must have / Should have / Could have / Won’t have). --- ## 2️⃣ Choose Your Tech Stack | Layer | Options | Pros | Cons | |-------|---------|------|------| | **Framework** | React, Vue, Angular, Svelte | Mature ecosystems, component reusability | Learning curve, bundle size | | **State Management** | Redux Toolkit, Zustand, Pinia, NgRx | Predictable state flow | Boilerplate overhead | | **Styling** | CSS Modules, Tailwind CSS, Styled‑Components, SCSS | Scoped styles, utility‑first | Runtime overhead (styled‑components) | | **Routing** | React Router, Vue Router, Angular Router | Declarative navigation | Requires code splitting | | **SSR / SSG** | Next.js, Nuxt.js, Remix, Astro | SEO + fast first paint | Build complexity | | **Build Tool** | Vite, Webpack, Rollup | Fast dev server, tree shaking | Configuration depth | | **Testing** | Jest + Testing Library, Cypress, Playwright | Unit + E2E coverage | Test maintenance effort | | **CI/CD** | GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI | Automation, reproducibility | Setup time | > **Recommendation:** For most e‑commerce sites, **Next.js (React)** or **Nuxt.js (Vue)** gives you SSR/SSG out of the box, which is great for SEO and performance. --- ## 3️⃣ Design System & UI Components 1. **Create a Design System** * Brand colors, typography, spacing scale, iconography. * Use Figma/Sketch/Adobe XD with shared libraries. 2. **Component Library** * Buttons, inputs, cards, modals, toast notifications, loading skeletons. * Keep components stateless where possible; let parent manage state. 3. **Accessibility First** * Semantic HTML (`
